title: FARDC-Wazalendo Retake Kibati and Milonge, AFC/M23 Holds Muhanga Heights
detail: A precarious calm settled over Kibati, Milonge and Muhanga in Walikale's Luberike grouping on Monday, Sept 14, a day after violent clashes there between FARDC-Wazalendo forces and AFC/M23 rebels. Administrative sources said FARDC and Wazalendo fighters regained control of the Kibati and Milonge town centers, while AFC/M23 remained entrenched on Mount Muhanga, a position considered strategically important overlooking the area. The human and material toll from the fighting remained unknown at this stage. Nearby Chanjikiro and Buhimba (Waloa Yungu grouping) also saw a fragile calm after two days of parallel clashes. Traffic on the Kashebere-Mungazi axis stayed suspended, and residents feared renewed fighting given the volatile situation.

media.caption: FARDC and Wazalendo forces regained the Kibati and Milonge town centers in Walikale as AFC/M23 held Mount Muhanga, Sept 14, 2026

confidenceReason: Reported by two Congolese outlets citing administrative sources; no FARDC or M23 statement and no casualty figures available.

title: Provincial Authorities Ban C64's Sept 15 March in Lubumbashi, Kananga, Kisangani; Coalition Vows to Proceed
detail: Ahead of the opposition Coalition Article 64's nationwide march planned for Sept 15 against Tshisekedi's constitutional referendum push, local authorities in several provinces moved to ban it. Lubumbashi's interim mayor Joyce Tunda banned the march on Sept 11, citing the need to 'preserve public order and social peace' and noting that public demonstrations were prohibited citywide; C64 rejected the order as unconstitutional, invoking Article 26's freedom-of-assembly guarantee and noting it had formally notified the mairie on Sept 7. Similar bans followed in Kananga (citing the suspension of political gatherings) and in Kisangani, where Tshopo governor Paulin Lendongolia invoked Ebola-related public-health restrictions on gatherings. Haut-Katanga police also barred the march. C64 said it would proceed regardless in Kinshasa, Lubumbashi and other cities, while in Lubumbashi Gen. Blaise Kilimbalimba placed troops on alert citing rising insecurity, and the National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) urged the march go forward as democratic expression rather than confrontation.

media.caption: C64 coalition supporters prepare to defy provincial bans on the planned Sept 15, 2026 march against Tshisekedi's constitutional referendum push

confidenceReason: Corroborated by Radio Okapi (tier 2) and Actualite.cd reporting the specific bans, officials' names and C64's public response.
